original_question: If K is an infinite weakly Radon-Nikodym compact space, meaning that K is homeomorphic to a weak*-compact subset of the dual of a Banach space not containing ℓ^1, must K contain a non-stationary convergent sequence?
target_in_paper: §1.2, Problem 1.5 (Haydon): "Does every WRN (infinite) compact admit a convergent (non-stationary) sequence?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it has the right quantifier form (an arbitrary infinite WRN compact space K), the right definition of WRN via weak*-compact subsets of duals of Banach spaces not containing ℓ^1, and the right conclusion, namely the existence of a convergent non-stationary sequence. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is an open problem, specifically Problem 1.5 in §1.2, and its exact wording is "Does every WRN (infinite) compact admit a convergent (non-stationary) sequence?" Aligning with that wording keeps the question closest to the source. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))

Under the paper’s standing conventions, all topological spaces are Hausdorff, so a fully stand-alone restatement should say that K is a compact Hausdorff space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
The Banach space in the WRN definition is, by the paper’s standing conventions, a real Banach space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))

In the paper’s terminology, saying a Banach space does not contain ℓ^1 means it contains no subspace isomorphic to ℓ^1; making that explicit removes hidden Banach-space shorthand. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))

For full self-containment, weak*-compact should be understood as compact with respect to the weak* topology on X*. The notation section fixes w* as the weak* topology on the dual. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))

The nearby context also notes the equivalent Banach-space description of the hypothesis: K is WRN exactly when C(K) is weakly precompactly generated (WPG). This is relevant context, even though Problem 1.5 itself is stated topologically. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
If one wants the question to be completely stand-alone for readers outside topology, it helps to gloss 'non-stationary' as 'not eventually constant.'
refined_question: Let K be an infinite compact Hausdorff space. Assume that K is weakly Radon-Nikodým, meaning that K is homeomorphic to a weak*-compact subset of X* for some real Banach space X that contains no subspace isomorphic to ℓ^1. Must K admit a convergent sequence that is non-stationary (that is, not eventually constant)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
justification: The closest official statement in arXiv:1607.07787 is Problem 1.5 in §1.2, and the paragraph immediately preceding it supplies the paper’s intended meaning of WRN and its relation to WPG. The notation section supplies the standing conventions needed to make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))
